Somewhere around 5 years ago, I splurged & bought myself 2 new pairs of casual sneakers, 2 pairs of casual "nice" shoes, and a nice pair of leather semi-formal shoes for work (in an office).

My price range was $30 - $90 per pair. Figured I'd get at least 5 years out of the set...

Now, the sneakers (despite being stored w/ an activated charcoal dessicant whenever not worn) smell pretty rancid, and their soles are worn away almost completely. What sole remains is separating from the rest of the shoe... And the stitching is starting to unravel, and the fabric to tear. The smell suffuses the fabric - no spray nor even the washing machine has been able to fully remove it.

The "casual nice" shoes (Sperry Topsiders) mostly fell apart or broke around year 1 & 2. Never buying that brand again...

The leather shoes - only ever worn to the office - are still in good physical shape, without too much sole wear, but looking pretty raggedy.

So, I got myself some new shoes again, but with a different strategy: just 2 pairs - one for the office each day, one for the rest of the time.

  • Made with real leather
  • Handmade (if possible)
  • Made in the USA (if possible)
  • I'll actually clean & condition them regularly & properly

I figure I can get at least 7 years this time, maybe 10.

I ended up choosing a pair of SAS (San Antonio Shoemakers) shoes, handmade in the USA, and a pair of Clark's, which are factory-made overseas, but are a "high-quality / boutique" brand.

I figured that would give me a good case-study of "handmade in USA" vs "high-end globalized" shoes.

I've already worn the "casual" shoes - the Clarks - and today's the first day with the new work shoes (SAS). I've got to say, thinking "handmade in the USA" gives me way more warm fuzzies than the (markedly cheaper, but just as nice-looking & comfortable) other pair. Way more than I thought it would.

If they hold up equally-well, in 7 to 10 years when it's time to replace again, I'm absolutely doing handmade in USA for both.

P.S. I've invested in leather shoe cleaning & care supplies, and am going to try to revitalize my old leather work shoes so I'll have a spare / alternate. They might be too neglected, though. Shame on me.
